title: Git Advanced Concepts - Module #19547
question: What is the purpose of the `git reflog` command in version control?
options: It logs the history of all local HEAD reference changes, allowing recovery of deleted commits or aborted rebases.
It lists all untracked files in class folders.
It displays the server pull logs from remote repository repositories.
It pushes local ref states to the main server branch.
answer: It logs the history of all local HEAD reference changes, allowing recovery of deleted commits or aborted rebases.
explanation: Git reflog tracks local checkouts, commits, rebases, and merges. Since git holds deleted commits in garbage collection for a period, reflog lets you retrieve their hashes.
